item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I may have missed this during the reading, but wouldn't the live feed also drive anyone monitoring 895 insane?

I don't see why so many people are hung up about the weight of the image tbh - it generates interest in a way a thousand words never could, and with significantly more effect than all the vivid descriptions and clever flourishes. It is based on a solid idea and tells me just enough that I know I would rather work with 173 than near this thing. The notion that like 096, you can't even really observe this SCP too closely without risking the lives of Foundation employees terrifies me.

Kudos to the author

Well, this comes to prove than as long a you have an excellent image, having an oustanding (Or even relatively nice idea) isn't really necessary. And I don't think that's good. The image is epic, yes, but you can't build an entire report over some piece of art that isn't even obligatory. There are a lot of really good scips that go unnoticed just because they aren't aestethically atractive, and that's a damn shame.

This needs a little improvement, I know the ruck of users couldn't care less, but it should be done, at least to justify the 470+ upvotes it received.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
We don't know exactly what happens when people see a live video feed of it when it's open - we just heard some noises that could have signified a number of extremely disturbing [DATA EXPUNGED]: internal organs forcing their way out of the viewers' mouths, the viewers' brains swelling and partially liquefying to go down the throat and push the eyeballs out of their sockets, some creepy monster clawing its way out of the viewers' chests…Use your imagination - that's typically the point of "[DATA EXPUNGED]" in an SCP. XD

As for the other "[DATA EXPUNGED]", I'm guessing the Foundation did a few tests to see if whatever happened during the recovery is exactly what happens every time someone views the coffin open through a video feed, and after they did that a few times, it got more powerful somehow and the "red zone" expanded.

Hmm…Now that I've thought about the article hard enough to write this comment, I see that it's really not lacking in terms of writing after all. XD
